rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the two barriers as the mountains of Armenia and Azerbaijan.
rows.anchor: روى عطاء الخراساني عن ابن عباس: «بين السدين» الجبلين أرمينية وأذربيجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min dunihima means from behind the two mountains.
rows.anchor: قوما لا يكادون يفقهون قولا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي والباقون
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the causative form, while the others read that the people themselves scarcely understand; both readings mean they neither understand nor make others understand.
rows.anchor: من أفقه إذا أبان أي لا يفقهون غيرهم كلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who speak to Dhu al-Qarnayn are a righteous human community.
rows.anchor: قالت له أمة من الإنس صالحة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: With hamza, Ya'juj follows the pattern yaf'ul and Ma'juj maf'ul, linked to the blaze of fire.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: من همز «يأجوج» فجعل الألفين من الأصل يقول: يأجوج يفعول ومأجوج مفعول

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Without hamza, the names may derive from yujj and mujj, with the two alifs treated as additions.
rows.anchor: قال: ومن لا يهمز ويجعل الألفين زائدتين يقول: «ياجوج» من يججت وماجوج من مججت

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ru'bah's verse attests the unhamzated form Yajuj.
rows.anchor: لو أن ياجوج وماجوج معا

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One view treats both names as foreign proper names, indeclinable like Talut and Jalut because of foreignness, definiteness, and femininity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما لم ينصرفا لأنهما اسمان أعجميان، مثل طالوت وجالوت

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another view derives the names as Arabized forms from ajj and ajjaj, with definiteness and femininity preventing declension.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هو معرب من أج وأجج علتاه في منع الصرف التعريف والتأنيث

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali allows Arabic derivations: Ya'juj from fire burning brightly, and Ma'juj as its passive participle; softened hamza or a derivation from majj is also possible.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي: يجوز أن يكونا عربيين فمن همز «يأجوج» فهو على وزن يفعول

rows.speaker: سعيد بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz says their corruption consisted of eating human beings.
rows.anchor: فقال سعيد بن عبد العزيز: إفسادهم أكل بني آدم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says the corruption was anticipated in the future, so the people sought protection in advance.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: إفسادهم إنما كان متوقعا، أي سيفسدون، فطلبوا وجه التحرز منهم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group understands corruption as familiar human wrongdoing, tyranny, oppression, killing, and other forms of harm.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: إفسادهم هو الظلم والغشم والقتل وسائر وجوه الإفساد المعلوم من البشر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra traces Ya'juj and Ma'juj to Japheth, alongside the lineages of Shem and Ham.
rows.anchor: يافث فولد سام العرب وفارس والروم والخير فيهم وولد يافث يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b says they arose from Adam's emission mixed with dust; al-Qurtubi rejects this because prophets do not have nocturnal emissions and affirms their descent from Japheth.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: احتلم آدم عليه السلام فاختلط ماؤه بالتراب فأسف فخلقوا من ذلك الماء

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet saying that no man among them dies before a thousand sons are born to him.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id says twenty-five tribes live beyond Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and men of these peoples likewise have a thousand sons before death.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد: هم خمس وعشرون قبيلة من وراء يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet describing two enormous nations, each with many subdivisions and armed male descendants, in three physical types that consume creatures and drink eastern rivers and Lake Tiberias.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali describes a small-clawed type, their digging and eventual escape from the barrier, bloodied arrows, and their death by neck parasites.
rows.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله تعالى عنه: وصنف منهم في طول شبر، لهم مخالب وأنياب السباع

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that Ya'juj and Ma'juj each have four hundred thousand leaders and that each man lives to see a thousand descendants as horsemen.
rows.anchor: أمة لها أربعمائة أمير وكذا مأجوج لا يموت أحدهم حتى ينظر إلى ألف فارس من ولده

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in Ibn Majah says they dig daily until the appointed time, then escape after saying inshaAllah; they drain water, their bloodied arrows deceive them, and parasites kill them, leaving animals to thrive on their flesh.
rows.anchor: إن يأجوج ومأجوج يحفران كل يوم حتى إذا كادوا يرون شعاع الشمس

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari explains shukr of a camel as its udder filling with milk.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: شكرت الناقة تشكر شكرا فهي شكرة وأشكر الضرع امتلأ لبنا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb describes their short stature, claws, predator teeth, hair, huge ears, and thousand offspring before death, male or female according to the parent.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: رآهم ذو القرنين، وطول الواحد منهم مثل نصف الرجل المربوع منا

rows.speaker: السدي والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Dahhak identify the Turks as a raiding remnant of Ya'juj and Ma'juj left outside the barrier; al-Suddi says it enclosed twenty-one tribes and left one outside, as Qatada also says.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي والضحاك: الترك شرذمة من يأجوج ومأجوج خرجت تغير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in Muslim and Abu Dawud predicts fighting with Turks, describing their shield-like faces and hair clothing or footwear.
rows.anchor: لا تقوم الساعة حتى يقاتل المسلمون الترك قوما وجوههم كالمجان المطرقة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Because of their number and strength, the Prophet said to leave the Turks alone as long as they leave Muslims alone.
rows.anchor: ولما علم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عددهم وكثرتهم وحدة شوكتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Turks of al-Qurtubi's time are too numerous to count and resemble Ya'juj and Ma'juj or their vanguard.
rows.anchor: وقد خرج منهم في هذا الوقت أمم لا يحصيهم إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Bakra's report predicts Banu Qantura arriving at Basra on the Tigris and dividing its inhabitants into three groups, including fighters who die as martyrs.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو داود عن أبي بكرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghait means low level ground, Basra takes its name from soft stones, and Banu Qantura are Turks descended from a servant woman of Abraham.
rows.anchor: الغائط المطمئن من الأرض. والبصرة الحجارة الرخوة وبها سميت البصرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offer of kharj is phrased as a polite question; kharj means payment and is narrower than kharaj.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فهل نجعل لك خرجا } استفهام على جهة حسن الأدب

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says kharaj can mean tax, public revenue, jizya, or yield, while kharj is the source noun for what is levied on property.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري: الخراج يقع على الضريبة، ويقع على مال الفيء، ويقع على الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested barrier is a rدم: material layered and joined until it forms a continuous barrier.
rows.anchor: والردم ما جعل بعضه على بعض حتى يتصل

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi explains that a patched garment is called mardum and that the verb means to close a breach.
rows.anchor: وثوب مردم أي مرقع، قاله الهروي. يقال: ردمت الثلمة أردمها بالكسر ردما أي سددتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rدم is stronger than sadd: it layers stone, earth, or similar material into an impenetrable barrier; the term also describes dense patching and layered poetic composition.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الردم أبلغ من السد إذ السد كل ما يسد به، والردم وضع الشيء

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh say sadd with damma is the noun and with fatha the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: فقال الخليل وسيبويه: الضم هو الاسم والفتح المصدر.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i treats the two vowelings of sadd as synonymous dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: الفتح والضم لغتان بمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They distinguish divinely formed barriers, read with damma, from human-made barriers, read with fatha; al-Qurtubi notes this would require inconsistent readings in the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيدة: ما كان من خلقة الله لم يشارك فيه أحد بعمل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة
rows.claim: Abu Hatim attributes to Ibn Abbas and Ikrima the reverse of Abu Ubayda's distinction.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم عن ابن عباس وعكرمة عكس ما قال أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq says visible barriers take damma and unseen ones fatha.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي إسحاق: ما رأته عيناك فهو سد بالضم، وما لا ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports establishing prisons and confining corrupt people to stop their harmful actions, with discipline, detention, surety, or release as Umar did.
rows.anchor: الثانية: في هذه الآية دليل على اتخاذ السجون، وحبس أهل الفساد فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn says God's grant of power and rule is better than their payment, and asks for physical labor and building materials instead.
rows.anchor: ما بسطه الله تعالى لي من القدرة والملك خير من خرجكم وأموالكم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir alone reads makkanī with two nuns; the remaining readers use the form with one nun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحده «ما مكنني» بنونين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruler must protect the people and repair defenses from public resources, prioritize need, avoid favoritism, distribute fairly, and require citizens' labor or resources only as necessity demands.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على أن الملك فرض عليه أن يقوم بحماية الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn prefers people to contribute their labor because taking their money would reduce resources needed for the work and the labor is faster.
rows.anchor: ورأى أن الأموال لا تغني عنهم، فإنه إن أخذها أجرة نقص ذلك مما يحتاج إليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When public funds are exhausted, citizens should contribute themselves before money is taken; any contribution is assessed and spent by considered judgment.
rows.anchor: فإذا فنيت بعد هذا وبقيت صفرا فأطلعت الحوادث أمرا بذلوا أنفسهم قبل أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubur are pieces of iron; Dhu al-Qarnayn requests their transfer and labor rather than a gift, having already declined payment.
rows.anchor: { زبر الحديد } قطع الحديد. وأصل الكلمة الاجتماع، ومنه زبرة الأسد

rows.speaker: أبو بكر والمفضل
rows.claim: They read radman i'tuni as a request to come with the iron, explaining the accusative by an omitted preposition, as in the cited poetic construction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر والمفضل «ردما ايتوني» من الإتيان الذي هو المجيء أي جيئوني بزبر الحديد،

rows.speaker: الحسن والجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read zubur with a fatha on the b, while al-Hasan uses damma; both are plurals of zubrah, a large piece.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «زبر» بفتح الباء. وقرأ الحسن بضمها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says the two sadafs are mountain sides facing one another; Zuhri and Ibn Abbas agree, and a poem supports the term.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: هما جانبا الجبل، وسميا بذلك لتصادفهما

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd uses sadaf and hadaf for any large, tall structure; a hadith describes a leaning sadaf.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: الصدف والهدف كل بناء عظيم مرتفع

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the two facing mountains are called sadafayn because each faces the other, not sadaf individually.
rows.anchor: ابن عطية: الصدفان الجبلان المتناوحان ولا يقال للواحد صدف، وإنما يقال صدفان

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read sadafayn with fatha and gemination; this is also Umar's and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's reading, preferred by Abu Ubayda as the best-known form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي «الصدفين» بفتح الصاد وشدها وفتح الدال

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read both consonants of sadafayn with damma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو «الصدفين» بضم الصاد والدال

rows.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر
rows.claim: Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission uses damma on sad and a quiescent dal, a shortened form like jurf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر «الصدفين» بضم الصاد وسكون الدال

rows.speaker: ابن الماجشون وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn al-Majishun and Qatada report additional vowelings; all readings refer to the two facing mountains.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الماجشون بفتح الصاد وضم الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Workers stack iron and stone, heat each layer with fuel and bellows until fiery, pour molten metal over it, then repeat until the structure becomes a solid mountain.
rows.anchor: ثم يوقد عليها الحطب والفحم بالمنافخ حتى تحمى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes the barrier as patterned cloth with black and red bands.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هو كالبرد المحبر، طريقة سوداء، وطريقة حمراء.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man told the Prophet he saw the barrier as yellow, red, and black bands; the Prophet replied that he had seen it.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جاءه رجل فقال: يا رسول الله إني رأيت سد يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the iron like fire means heating it until it is fire-like; the instruction to bring qitr is fronted relative to the pouring action.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { حتى إذا جعله نارا } أي كالنار. ومعنى { آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand qitr as molten copper, named for dripping as it melts; other views identify it as molten iron or lead.
rows.anchor: والقطر عند أكثر المفسرين النحاس المذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who read i'tuni understand the command as 'come so I may pour copper over it.'
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ «ائتوني» فالمعنى عنده تعالوا أفرغ عليه نحاسا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ya'juj and Ma'juj cannot climb the barrier because its surface is smooth and level with the high mountain.
rows.anchor: أي ما استطاع يأجوج ومأجوج أن يعلوه ويصعدوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier is said to be 250 cubits high; Wahb reports a length of 100 farsakhs and width of 50.
rows.anchor: وارتفاع السد مائتا ذراع وخمسون ذراعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot breach it because it is too wide and strong.
rows.anchor: لبعد عرضه وقوته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: An authentic Abu Hurayra report says an opening of this size had been made in the barrier; Wahb demonstrated about ninety with his hand, and another version indicates the thumb and next finger.
rows.anchor: وروي في الصحيح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report through Qatada says they dig daily; at the appointed time they say inshaAllah, find the opening as left, and emerge among people.
rows.anchor: وذكر يحيى بن سلام عن سعد بن أبي عروبة عن قتادة عن أبي رافع عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has a light ṭ; some treat it as a dialectal shortening of istata'u, while others note ordinary deletion of ta or ṭa in Arabic.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فما اسطاعوا } بتخفيف الطاء على قراءة الجمهور. وقيل: هي لغة بمعنى استطاعوا.

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza alone doubles ṭ by assimilating the ta of istata'u; Abu Ali considers this reading invalid or weakly justified.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحده «فما اسطاعوا» بتشديد الطاء كأنه أراد استطاعوا،

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reads istata'u with ta in both clauses.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «فما استطاعوا أن يظهروه وما استطاعوا له نقبا» بالتاء في الموضعين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn points to the barrier as a mercy from God, including its strength and its benefit in warding off Ya'juj and Ma'juj.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قال هذا رحمة من ربي } القائل ذو القرنين، وأشار بهذا إلى الردم

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads the demonstrative in the feminine: hadhihi rahmatun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «هذه رحمة من ربي».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised time means the Day of Resurrection, though another view says it is the time when Ya'juj and Ma'juj emerge.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فإذا جاء وعد ربي } أي يوم القيامة. وقيل: وقت خروجهم.

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn Arfa explains dakkā as making the earth level, without any mound.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عرفة: أي جعلت مستوية لا أكمة فيها، ومنه قوله تعالى: «جعله دكا»

rows.speaker: اليزيدي
rows.claim: Al-Yazidi explains dakkā as level and compares it to a camel that has lost its hump.
rows.anchor: قال اليزيدي: أي مستويا يقال: ناقة دكاء إذا ذهب سنامها.

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutbi says the barrier is crushed and brought flush with the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال القتبي: أي جعله مدكوكا ملصقا بالأرض.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes dakkā as fragments broken apart and cites a poetic line about collapse.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قطعا متكسرا قال: هل غير غاد دك غارا فانهدم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari connects the word to pounding or crushing something.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري: يقال دككته أي دققته.

rows.speaker: حمزة وعاصم والكسائي
rows.claim: They read dakkā' long, as a flat mound or a camel without a hump; the feminine form requires an understood comparison because the barrier is masculine.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وعاصم والكسائي «دكاء» بالمد على التشبيه بالناقة الدكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The short reading dakkan can be a verbal noun meaning demolishing or can be accusative of state, including with the long reading; the Lord's promise is true.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ «دكا» فهو مصدر دك يدك إذا هدم ورض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If believers imitate disbelievers' indulgent eating, their claim to faith is hollow; excess eating increases greed and brings idleness and sleep.
rows.anchor: والذين كفروا يتمتعون ويأكلون كما تأكل الأنعام والنار مثوى لهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When people laughed at Ibn Mas'ud's thin legs as he climbed a palm, the Prophet said that a leg weighed by deeds is weightier than the earth.
rows.anchor: تضحكون من ساق توزن بعمل أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says he already explained the balance and its pans weighing records in al-A'raf, so need not repeat it.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في «الأعراف» هذا المعنى وتقدم فيها ذكر الميزان، وأن له كفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, 'that' refers to abandoning the weighing; 'their recompense' is its predicate, Hell is apposition, and 'what' in 'for what they disbelieved' is a verbal noun marker.
rows.anchor: «ذلك» إشارة إلى ترك الوزن، وهو في موضع رفع بالابتداء «جزاؤهم» خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huz' means contempt and mockery.
rows.anchor: والهزء الاستخفاف والسخرية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada locates Firdaus on a high hill, at the center and summit of Paradise, and calls it its best and highest part.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: الفردوس ربوة الجنة وأوسطها وأعلاها وأفضلها

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
rows.claim: Abu Umama al-Bahili calls Firdaus the center of Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو أمامة الباهلي: الفردوس سرة الجنة.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says no garden is above Firdaus and that it contains those who command right and forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: ليس في الجنان جنة أعلى من جنة الفردوس فيها الآمرون بالمعروف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra's Bukhari report promises Paradise to those who believe, pray, and fast; it describes a hundred ranks for fighters and says to ask for Firdaus, the highest central garden above which is the Throne and from which rivers flow.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Firdaus means garden in Roman usage.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: والفردوس البستان بالرومية.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Firdaus is Arabic and denotes a garden in Paradise.
rows.anchor: الفراء: هو عربي. والفردوس حديقة في الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording describes the dwellers as remaining in Paradise and not seeking a change of place; hawl may mean transfer, or a stratagem for changing one’s place.
rows.anchor: { خالدين فيها } أي دائمين. { لا يبغون عنها حولا } أي لا يطلبون تحويلا عنها إلى غيرها.

rows.speaker: أبو علي والزجاج
rows.claim: Abu Ali glosses hawl as transfer; al-Zajjaj explains it as a verbal noun like greatness from great.
rows.anchor: والحول بمعنى التحويل قاله أبو علي. وقال الزجاج: حال من مكانه حولا كما يقال: عظم عظما.

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari says tahawwul is moving from one place to another and hawl is its noun.
rows.anchor: وقال الجوهري: التحول التنقل من موضع إلى موضع، والاسم الحول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the sea were ink for the words of God, it would run out before His words; more seas would add to it, and Ubayy’s codex and several readers have madadan.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي } نفد الشيء إذا تم وفرغ وقد تقدم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews asked how the Prophet could say they had little knowledge when they had received the Torah; the verse answered that Torah and Quran are slight beside the words of God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: قالت اليهود لما قال لهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم { وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا } قالوا: وكيف وقد أوتينا التوراة،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the words of God as His admonitions.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «لكلمات ربي» أي مواعظ ربي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes God’s words as eternal speech without end; although one, it may be expressed in the plural for its many distinct utterances and by way of magnification.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عنى بالكلمات الكلام القديم الذي لا غاية له ولا منتهى، وهو وإن كان واحدا فيجوز أن يعبر عنه بلفظ الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet knows only what God teaches him and is commanded to convey that God alone is deity; hope of meeting God includes hoping for vision and reward and fearing punishment.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي } أي لا أعلم إلا ما يعلمني الله تعالى،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Jundub ibn Zuhayr, who did deeds for God but liked others to notice; the Prophet said God accepts only what is purely for Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في جندب بن زهير العامري، قال:

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus reports a man who loved jihad for God but also wanted his position to be seen; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال طاوس قال رجل: يا رسول الله! إني أحب الجهاد في سبيل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports a man who gave charity and maintained kinship for God but felt pleased when praised; after the Prophet fell silent, the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: جاء رجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says all these occasions are intended, and the verse covers them and every other kind of deed.
rows.anchor: قلت: والكل مراد، والآية تعم ذلك كله وغيره من الأعمال.

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says all exegetes understand 'associate no one in worship' as forbidding showiness in one's deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال الماوردي وقال جميع أهل التأويل: معنى قوله تعالى: { ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا } إنه لا يرائي بعمله أحدا.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets God's words as descriptions of Paradise, which would outlast every sea used as ink.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: أي إن كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد صفات الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman 27 is a parallel image of God's words remaining inexhaustible even if the earth's trees became pens and seven seas supplied ink.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية ولو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the verb before 'words' with ya, matching its preceding verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «قبل أن ينفد» بالياء لتقدم الفعل.

rows.speaker: عبادة بن نسي عن شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: Shaddad reports the Prophet's fear for his community of subtle shirk and hidden desire: they show off deeds rather than worship idols, and a fasting person may break fast for worldly desire.
rows.anchor: عن عبادة بن نسي قال: أتيت شداد بن أوس في مصلاه وهو يبكي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says ostentation is shirk and cites the verse forbidding association in worship.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الواحد: فلقيت الحسن، فقلت: يا أبا سعيد! أخبرني عن الرياء أشرك هو؟ قال: نعم

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت وشداد بن أوس
rows.claim: They say they fear hidden shirk and desire, interpret the desire as involving women, and transmit the Prophet's warning that prayer or fasting done for show is shirk.
rows.anchor: فقالا: إنا نتخوف على هذه الأمة من الشرك والشهوة الخفية، فأما الشهوة الخفية فمن قبل النساء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says hidden desire has also been interpreted differently, with discussion in his commentary on al-Nisa'.
rows.anchor: قلت: وقد جاء تفسير الشهوة الخفية بخلاف هذا، وقد ذكرناه في «النساء».

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan defines sincerity as liking to conceal good deeds and disliking concealment of sins; if good deeds are exposed, one credits God's grace rather than oneself.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله: وسئل الحسن عن الإخلاص والرياء فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who give what they give in 23:60 are sincere yet fear their deeds will not be accepted; ostentation seeks worldly benefit, and any aim besides God's face and the afterlife is showiness.
rows.anchor: الآية يؤتون الإخلاص، وهم يخافون ألا يقبل منهم

rows.speaker: طاهر بن الحسين وأبو عبد الله المروزي
rows.claim: A story mocks ostentatious self-praise: a man answers a question about arriving in Iraq by boasting he had fasted for thirty years.
rows.anchor: كما يحكى أن طاهر بن الحسين قال لأبي عبد الله المروزي: منذ كم صرت إلى العراق

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i tells of a Bedouin who lengthened prayer for an audience and then added that he was fasting when praised.
rows.anchor: وحكى الأصمعي أن أعرابيا صلى فأطال وإلى جانبه قوم

rows.speaker: الأشعث بن قيس
rows.claim: Al-Ash'ath says his shortened prayer contained no ostentation, avoiding both show and the audience's taunts.
rows.anchor: أين هذا من قول الأشعث بن قيس وقد صلى فخفف، فقيل له إنك خففت فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi points to the remedy for ostentation attributed to Luqman in al-Nisa': concealing one's action.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في «النساء» دواء الرياء من قول لقمان وأنه كتمان العمل.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report witnessed by Abu Bakr says shirk can be more hidden than an ant's movement and teaches seeking refuge from known and unknown association three times.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر وشهد به على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال:

rows.speaker: معاوية
rows.claim: Umar ibn Qays al-Kindi says Mu'awiya recited this verse from the pulpit and called it the last verse sent from heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن قيس الكندي سمعت معاوية تلا هذه الآية على المنبر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Umar transmits a report promising light from Aden to Mecca, with angels praying and seeking forgiveness, for one who recites the verse about righteous work.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Mu'adh ibn Jabal reports that reciting the beginning and end of al-Kahf gives light from head to foot, and the whole surah light from earth to heaven.
rows.anchor: وقال معاذ بن جبل قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas tells a man who fears oversleeping to recite the closing passage of al-Kahf before bed; God will wake him whenever he wishes.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال له رجل: إني أضمر أن أقوم ساعة من الليل

rows.speaker: زر بن حبيش
rows.claim: A report in al-Darimi says whoever recites the end of al-Kahf intending to rise at night will do so; Abdah says they tested it and found it true.
rows.anchor: وفي مسند الدارمي أبي محمد أخبرنا محمد بن كثير عن الأوزاعي عن عبدة عن زر بن حبيش قال:

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi quotes al-Tartushi advising against wasting time fighting peers and maintaining friends, and notes the surah closes with the call to sincere righteous work.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: كان شيخنا الطرطوشي الأكبر يقول:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the opening letters as divine attributes: sufficient, guiding, wise, knowing, and truthful, with each letter pointing to a name.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في { كهيعص }: إن الكاف من كاف، والهاء من هاد، والياء من حكيم،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi offers another expansion: generous, great, sufficient; guiding; merciful; knowing and mighty; truthful.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي أيضا: الكاف من كريم وكبير وكاف، والهاء من هاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the letters form one of God's names.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: هو اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali calls it God's name and would invoke it in a prayer for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه هو اسم الله عز وجل وكان يقول: يا كهيعص اغفر لي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi calls it God's greatest name, by which a prayer is answered.
rows.anchor: السدي: هو اسم الله الأعظم الذي إذا سئل به أعطى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it is a name of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قتادة: هو اسم من أسماء القرآن

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri prefers the view that the letters name the surah, making the phrase complete like a book or chapter heading.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم للسورة وهو اختيار القشيري في أوائل الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ja'far reads the letters separately while the others connect them; readers differ over imala, opening, and intermediate vowel quality for ha and ya.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن جعفر هذه الحروف متقطعة، ووصلها الباقون

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو حاتم وهارون القارئ
rows.claim: Hasan's reported damma readings were rejected by Abu Hatim, but Harun explains them as a slight rounding gesture, like dialectal pronunciation of salat and zakat.
rows.anchor: وحكى إسماعيل بن إسحاق أنه كان يضم يا. قال أبو حاتم: ولا يجوز ضم الكاف

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the dal of the spelled letter sad distinctly; others assimilate it, and this articulation is Abu Ubayd's choice.
rows.anchor: وأظهر الدال من هجاء «ص» نافع وابن كثير وعاصم ويعقوب، وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farra makes dhikr grammatically governed by the opening letters; al-Zajjaj rejects this because those letters do not narrate Zechariah's story.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: هو مرفوع ب«كهيعص» قال الزجاج: هذا محال

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies an implied phrase: what is being recited to you is the mention of your Lord's mercy.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: التقدير فيما يقص عليكم ذكر رحمة ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing takes the phrase to mean that this recitation is the mention of your Lord's mercy.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث: أن المعنى هذا الذي يتلوه عليكم ذكر رحمة ربك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implied subject can make 'dhikr rahmat rabbik' mean 'this is the mention of your Lord's mercy'; al-Hasan reads it as the Qur'an's mention of that mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «ذكر رحمة ربك» رفع بإضمار مبتدأ أي هذا ذكر رحمة ربك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads dhikr as a declarative clarification that the recited Qur'an is the mention of God's mercy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: «ذكر رحمة ربك» أي هذا المتلو من القرآن ذكر رحمة ربك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imperative reading is also reported; grammarians agree that the feminine ending is written and paused on as ha to distinguish feminine nouns from verbs.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ذكر» على الأمر. «ورحمة» تكتب ويوقف عليها بالهاء

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says 'his servant' is accusative through rahma, with Zechariah as its apposition.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: هو منصوب ب«رحمة». «زكريا» بدل منه

rows.speaker: الزجاج والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Farra propose fronting and postponement: the Lord mentions Zechariah his servant with mercy, making servant accusative through dhikr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو على التقديم والتأخير معناه: ذكر ربك عبده زكريا برحمة

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya reads 'his servant Zechariah' in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم «عبده زكريا» بالرفع وهي قراءة أبي العالية.

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Ya'mar reads dhikra in the accusative, meaning this Qur'an mentions mercy upon Zechariah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر «ذكر» بالنصب على معنى هذا القرآن ذكر رحمة عبده زكريا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nida' is supplication and longing; Zechariah privately addressed God in his prayer chamber, as shown by the account of the angels calling him while he prayed.
rows.anchor: والنداء الدعاء والرغبة أي ناجى ربه بذلك في محرابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible reasons for hiding the prayer include avoiding blame, sincerity, avoiding ostentation, or praying secretly at night; al-Qurtubi says the first is clearest, while secrecy in supplication is commendable.
rows.anchor: واختلف في إخفائه هذا النداء فقيل: أخفاه من قومه لئلا يلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas says the best remembrance is hidden and the best provision is what suffices.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: يونس بن عبيد
rows.claim: Yunus says al-Hasan favored silent qunut by the imam and silent amens from those behind, citing Zechariah's hidden prayer.
rows.anchor: قال يونس بن عبيد: كان الحسن يرى أن يدعو الإمام في القنوت

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Malik made qunut quiet and al-Shafi'i loud; loudness is preferable because the Prophet prayed it aloud.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد أسر مالك القنوت وجهر به الشافعي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahana is read with three vowel patterns and means weakness; the bone is singular because it is the body's pillar, whose weakening causes the rest of its strength to collapse.
rows.anchor: قرىء «وهن» بالحركات الثلاث أي ضعف. يقال: وهن يهن وهنا إذا ضعف

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd gives alternate verb forms for expressing weakness.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد يقال: وهن يهن ووهن يوهن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular bone denotes the whole bodily frame and emphasizes that its central support has weakened; a plural would instead emphasize every bone.
rows.anchor: ووحده لأن الواحد هو الدال على معنى الجنسية

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the sin of ishta'ala into the shin.
rows.anchor: أدغم السين في الشين أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spreading of white hair is beautifully compared to flames spreading; the head names the hair's location, and shayban is either a verbal noun or specification, with al-Nahhas preferring the former analysis.
rows.anchor: وهذا من أحسن الاستعارة في كلام العرب. والاشتعال انتشار شعاع النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplicants should mention God's blessings and express humility: the weakened bones show humility, while Zechariah recalls that God has always answered his prayers.
rows.anchor: الثالثة: قال العلماء: يستحب للمرء أن يذكر في دعائه نعم الله تعالى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression 'I was never disappointed in my prayer' means God never frustrated his request and had habitually answered him; a needy person's appeal to past generosity illustrates this form of supplication.
rows.anchor: أي لم تكن تخيب دعائي إذا دعوتك أي إنك عودتني الإجابة فيما مضى

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان ومحمد بن علي وعلي بن الحسين ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They read khift with fatḥa and a doubled f, making the relatives the subject: they have dwindled through death.
rows.anchor: قرأ عثمان بن عفان ومحمد بن علي وعلي بن الحسين ويحيى بن يعمر رضي الله تعالى عنهم «خفت» بفتح الخاء وتشديد الفاء وكسر التاء وسكون الياء من «الموالي» لأنه في موضع رفع «بخفت» ومعناه انقطعت أي بالموت.

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use khift with kasra and treat the relatives as the object: Zechariah fears them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «خفت» بكسر الخاء وسكون الفاء وضم التاء ونصب الياء من «الموالي» لأنه في موضع نصب ب«خفت».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawali here means relatives, cousins, and agnates; Arabs also call paternal cousins mawali, as a poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: و«الموالي» هنا الأقارب وبنو العم والعصبة الذين يلونه في النسب.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They say Zechariah feared relatives inheriting his property and was concerned that collateral kin would inherit without a child.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة: خاف أن يرثوا ماله وأن ترثه الكلالة

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group says his relatives neglected religion, so he feared religious practice would be lost after his death; al-Qurtubi prefers this view because prophets leave no inheritance.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: إنما كان مواليه مهملين للدين فخاف بموته أن يضيع الدين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says prophets do not inherit; whatever they leave is alms, supporting the interpretation that Zechariah sought an heir in knowledge and prophethood rather than wealth.
rows.anchor: لما ثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Dawud's report says scholars inherit the prophets' knowledge, not dinars or dirhams.
rows.anchor: إن العلماء ورثة الأنبياء وأن الأنبياء لم يورثوا دينارا ولا درهما ورثوا العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report construes Solomon's inheritance of David in 27:16 as wisdom and knowledge, and Zechariah's request as inheritance of knowledge from Jacob's family; al-Qurtubi rejects contrary views as conflicting with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الثانية: هذا الحديث يدخل في التفسير المسند لقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says 'inherit me' refers to wealth, while inheritance from Jacob's family means prophethood and wisdom.
rows.anchor: ما عدا الروافض، وإلا ما روي عن الحسن أنه قال:

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says most exegetes understood Zechariah to seek property, and suggests the Prophet's hadith may describe the usual rather than universal case; al-Qurtubi finds knowledge and religion more fitting.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والأكثر من المفسرين على أن زكريا إنما أراد وراثة المال

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says Jacob's family means knowledge and prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح وغيره: قوله «من آل يعقوب» يريد العلم والنبوة.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads min wara'i with lengthening and hamza, and also transmits a shortened form with open ya; the others lengthen and quiesce ya.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير بالمد والهمز وفتح الياء

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: Uthman's khift reading is very unusual; critics object it means fearing relatives while alive, while al-Nahhas offers a distant-time interpretation and Ibn Atiyya takes it as after his death.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة شاذة بعيدة جدا حتى زعم بعض العلماء أنها لا تجوز

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari identifies Zechariah's wife as Ishaa daughter of Faqudha ibn Qabil and Hannah's sister; Hannah was Mary's mother.
rows.anchor: امرأته هي إيشاع بنت فاقوذا بن قبيل، وهي أخت حنة بنت فاقوذا قاله الطبري.

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutbi identifies Zechariah's wife as Ishaa daughter of Imran, making John and Jesus literal maternal cousins; the other genealogy makes John cousin of Mary's mother, while the Isra' hadith supports the first view.
rows.anchor: وقال القتبي: امرأة زكريا هي إيشاع بنت عمران،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaqir describes a woman unable to bear from old age or other barrenness, and can also describe an infertile man; 42:50 is cited along with a line by Amir ibn al-Tufayl.
rows.anchor: والعاقر التي لا تلد لكبر سنها وقد مضى بيانه في «آل عمران».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah asks for a guardian without explicitly saying child, knowing his wife's condition and the remoteness of that possibility.
rows.anchor: سؤال ودعاء. ولم يصرح بولد لما علم من حاله وبعده عنه بسبب المرأة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada dates Zechariah's prayer to age seventy-something; Muqatil says ninety-five, which al-Qurtubi considers more plausible given their circumstances and the mention of advanced age.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: جرى له هذا الأمر وهو ابن بضع وسبعين سنة.

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group says he asked for a child and also to live long enough to inherit, in case the child died before fulfilling that purpose.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: بل طلب الولد، ثم طلب أن تكون الإجابة في أن يعيش حتى يرثه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request aimed to preserve religion and prophethood and increase reward, not worldly benefit; Zechariah's prayer invokes God's past generosity.
rows.anchor: السادسة: قال العلماء: دعاء زكريا عليه السلام في الولد إنما كان لإظهار دينه

rows.speaker: حاتم
rows.claim: An anecdote about Hatim illustrates appealing to a benefactor by reminding him of his past generosity.
rows.anchor: يروى أن حاتم الجود لقيه رجل فسأله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet may ask for an extraordinary favor in the era of miracles; Mary's miraculous provision increased Zechariah's hope and led to his prayer for good offspring.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: كيف أقدم زكريا على مسألة ما يخرق العادة دون إذن؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah saw the extraordinary provision given to Mary and grew more hopeful of an answered prayer; he then asked God for good offspring.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى خارق العادة استحكم طمعه في إجابة دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although wealth and children can be trials or enemies, prayer for children is supported by revelation; Zechariah asks for pure offspring and a pleasing child, who benefits parents in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: السابعة: إن قال قائل: هذه الآية تدل على جواز الدعاء بالولد، والله سبحانه وتعالى قد حذرنا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that Anas receive abundant wealth and children and blessing, guarding against harm that abundance could bring.
rows.anchor: دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنس خادمه فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer should pray for a child's guidance and salvation in this life and the next, following the prophets and righteous saints.
rows.anchor: وهكذا فليتضرع العبد إلى مولاه في هداية ولده، ونجاته في أولاه وأخراه

rows.speaker: أهل الحرمين والحسن وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: They read yarithuni and yarithu in the nominative; Yahya ibn Ya'mar and others read both in the jussive. Sibawayh's implied conditional supports the jussive, while the nominative better specifies the heir requested; Abu Ubayd objects to the conditional and al-Nahhas answers that command clauses imply condition.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحرمين والحسن وعاصم وحمزة «يرثني ويرث» بالرفع فيهما.

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas lists three interpretations of inheritance: prophethood, wisdom, or property; he rejects inherited prophethood, favors knowledge and wisdom, and says property is not impossible despite objections from the hadith.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: فأما معنى { يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب } فللعلماء فيه ثلاثة أجوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of the prophetic hadith is that the Prophet's estate was already charity; another takes Allah's grant from spoils as the Prophet's life-long provision and reads the hadith accordingly.
rows.anchor: وقد يؤول هذا بمعنى لا نورث الذي تركنا صدقة

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar gives two readings of 'we do not inherit what we leave is charity': the majority say prophets are not inherited and their residue is alms; some Basrans say the Prophet was specially granted that all his property be charity, like his unique marital rulings.
rows.anchor: على قولين: أحدهما: وهو الأكثر وعليه الجمهور أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يورث وما ترك صدقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob may mean Israel: Mary's line descends through David and Judah, while Zechariah descends through Aaron and Levi; prophecy was among Jacob's descendants.
rows.anchor: الثالثة: قوله تعالى: { من آل يعقوب } قيل: هو يعقوب إسرائيل، وكان زكريا متزوجا بأخت مريم بنت عمران

rows.speaker: مقاتل وغيره
rows.claim: Another view identifies Jacob as Jacob ibn Mathan, brother of Mary's father Imran; their family descended from Solomon and led the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعني بيعقوب هاهنا يعقوب بن ماثان أخو عمران بن ماثان أبي مريم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Jacob ibn Mathan was Zechariah's maternal uncle and had kingship; Zechariah descended from Aaron.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: وكان آل يعقوب أخواله، وهو يعقوب بن ماثان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet's prayer for mercy on Zechariah, remarking on the number of heirs he had.
rows.anchor: وروى قتادة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqub is indeclinable because it is a foreign name.
rows.anchor: ولم ينصرف يعقوب لأنه أعجمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Radiyyan may mean morally pleasing and approved, content with God's decree, or a righteous man God approves; Abu Salih says it means a prophet.
rows.anchor: أي مرضيا في أخلاقه وأفعاله. وقيل: راضيا بقضائك وقدرك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glad tidings imply God's answer to prayer, the gift of a son, and the honor of God naming him.
rows.anchor: فتضمنت هذه البشرى ثلاثة أشياء: أحدها: إجابة دعائه وهي كرامة.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Yahya was named because he came alive between an elderly father and mother; al-Qurtubi questions this because his wife was barren, not merely old.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: سماه يحيى لأنه حيي بين أب شيخ وأم عجوز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن أسلم والسدي
rows.claim: They say no one had previously been named Yahya; God's naming is also a favor rather than leaving the choice to the parents.
rows.anchor: لم نسم أحدا قبل يحيى بهذا الاسم قاله ابن عباس وقتادة وابن أسلم والسدي.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others interpret samiyyan as equal or counterpart, as in 19:65; al-Qurtubi finds this far-fetched unless Yahya is uniquely distinguished in leadership or continence.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: { سميا } معناه مثلا ونظيرا،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains that no barren woman had previously borne a child like Yahya.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: معناه لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says 'before' is specified because Muhammad, who is greater, would be created after Yahya.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى اشترط القبل، لأنه أراد أن يخلق بعده أفضل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text favors noble, distinctive names because they are more memorable and less open to insulting nicknames; a poem and a genealogy anecdote illustrate this.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل وشاهد على أن الأسامي السنع جديرة بالأثرة، وإياها كانت العرب تنتحي في التسمية لكونها أنبه وأنزه عن النبز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah asks in amazement at God's power, not in rejection of the glad tidings: a child would come from a barren woman and an elderly man.
rows.anchor: ليس على معنى الإنكار لما أخبر الله تعالى به، بل على سبيل التعجب من قدرة الله تعالى أن يخرج ولدا من امرأة عاقر وشيخ كبير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atiyya means the endpoint of old age, dryness, and hardness; its root has waw, replaced by ya as a lighter sibling and to fit the verse endings.
rows.anchor: يعني النهاية في الكبر واليبس والجفاف ومثله العسي قال الأصمعي:

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i explains asa as becoming dry and hard, and describes the aging verb forms.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي: عسا الشيء يعس عسوا وعساء ممدود أي يبس وصلب،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads asiyyan, as in Ubayy's codex; Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs use kasra for atiyyan and related forms, while other vowel patterns are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «عسيا» وهو كذلك في مصحف أبي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atiyyan may also mean harsh or hard-hearted, as in a cruel king.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «عتيا» قسيا يقال: ملك عات إذا كان قاسي القلب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel says the matter is as stated by God; the kaaf functions as a predicate, meaning that creating Yahya is easy for Him.
rows.anchor: أي قال له الملك «كذلك قال ربك» والكاف في موضع رفع أي الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra paraphrases the statement as: creating him is easy for Me.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: خلقه علي هين.

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة وعاصم
rows.claim: They read 'I created you before'; the other Kufans read 'We created you' with plural of majesty, and the first matches the written consonantal text more closely.
rows.anchor: وهذه قراءة أهل المدينة والبصرة وعاصم. وقرأ سائر الكوفيين «وقد خلقناك».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not being anything means nonexistence before creation, demonstrating God's power to create Yahya.
rows.anchor: أي كما خلقك الله تعالى بعد العدم ولم تك شيئا موجودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah asks for a sign after the promise and reminder of his own creation to gain further reassurance and complete the favor.
rows.anchor: طلب آية على حملها بعد بشارة الملائكة إياه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Zechariah sought proof that the promise came from God rather than Satan; al-Qurtubi questions this because the text already says angels called him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: طلب آية تدله على أن البشرى منه بيحيى لا من الشيطان
